ecoa_prohibited_basis_disclosure: The Federal Equal Credit Opportunity Act prohibits creditors from discriminating against credit applicants on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (provided the applicant has the capacity to enter into a binding contract); because all or part of the applicant's income derives from any public assistance program; or because the applicant has in good faith exercised any right under the Consumer Credit Protection Act. The Federal agency that administers compliance with this law concerning this creditor is [Federal agency name and address].
fcra_consumer_reporting_agency_disclosur: You have the right to request a free copy of your consumer report from the consumer reporting agency that furnished the report within 60 days. You also have the right to dispute the accuracy or completeness of any information in your consumer report by contacting the consumer reporting agency directly.
credit_score_disclosure_text: A numerical credit score, your credit score, the credit score range used, the date the credit score was created, and the name of the consumer reporting agency or other person that provided the credit score are provided above. The credit score is a numerical value derived from a statistical model that uses information from a consumer reporting agency to predict the likelihood of repayment. The credit score ranges from 300 to 850; higher scores indicate lower credit risk.
right_to_obtain_credit_score_text: You have the right to obtain a free copy of your credit score from the consumer reporting agency that furnished the credit score within 60 days of this notice. You may also request a free credit file disclosure from the consumer reporting agency in accordance with section 612 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. §1681j).
